title: Metric proxy: OTLP -> Prometheus routing with per-tenant sticky sampling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a lightweight metric-proxy layer that accepts OTLP metrics from inference workers and routes them to either the Prometheus scrape-compatible pipeline or our downstream telemetry fabric depending on tenant and metric type. Goals: 1) support legacy Prometheus-style exporters from some components while consolidating enriched OTLP metrics; 2) implement per-tenant sticky sampling for high-cardinality inference KPIs (model_id, route_id, prompt_family) to keep SLO-aligned signal while bounding cardinality; 3) add a mode that emits both Prometheus counters (for console dashboards) and OTLP envelopes (for long-term aggregation). This ticket covers design, implementation, rollout plan, dashboards, and a follow-up migration plan for consumer teams.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP metrics and tags them with tenant_id, model_id, route_id
Configurable routing rules exist: (a) route to prometheus-exporter (scrape) OR (b) forward to telemetry-fabric OTLP gateway
Sticky sampling implemented per-tenant with deterministic selection based on trace_id/model_id and a configurable sample_rate
Proxy exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics for its own health and backpressure signals
E2E latency for metric forwarding < 200ms p95 under normal load
No regression in existing dashboards: console latency/error dashboard queries return baseline with proxy enabled
Migration playbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence with owner and runbook links
work_items: Design meeting with applied-ml and infra to sketch sampling keys and default rates
Define routing DSL and config schema for tenant-based rules
Prototype proxy in Go using OTLP receiver (gRPC) + Prometheus exporter client
Implement sticky-sampling module with seeded hashing and admit-list overrides
Add metrics and tracing hooks for observability (span per-forward, backpressure counters)
Performance testing in staging with synthetic high-cardinality workloads
Create dashboards and alerting rules for dropped samples and queue latency
Gradual rollout via canary: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with monitored SLOs
Docs: Confluence design doc, runbook, and SDK/agent configuration examples
